SBP: I told the patient that I would be communicating what they had told me to my supervisor, an attending physician, who would subsequently be continuing the discussion with them.
ICS: I identified myself to the patient by my surname and professional role (medical student).
I addressed the patient by their surname.
I spoke in language easily understandable to the patient.
I used smooth, appropriate transitions and seemed organized.
I listened carefully to the patient.
I brought the encounter to a close.
I confirmed that the patient understood what I intended to do for them.
I think that this patient trusts, or has confidence, that I will help them.
I think the patient will do, or adhere to, what I ask them to do.
I think that this patient would be willing to return to me for care in the future.
Overall, I think the patient was satisfied with care I provided to them.
PROF: I treated the patient with respect.
I demonstrated care for the patient and their health.
